title: A Fantasy of Fashion: Articles of Interest #7

sentences.zh: 这里是“隐形百分之九十九”。

sentences.en: Man is a perpetually wanting animal.
sentences.zh: 人是一种永不知足的动物。

sentences.en: These are the words of Abraham Maslow, the psychologist,
sentences.zh: 这是心理学家亚伯拉罕·马斯洛的话，

sentences.en: who in 1943 identified that humans have five basic needs.
sentences.zh: 他在1943年指出人类有五种基本需求。

sentences.en: On the first and most basic level is the physiological need for food and water.
sentences.zh: 最初也是最基础的层面是对食物和水等生理需求。

sentences.en: The second need is shelter, a sense of safety and security.
sentences.zh: 第二种需求是庇护所、安全感和保障。
那是制片人艾弗里·特拉夫曼。

sentences.en: The third level is the need for love and belonging.
sentences.zh: 第三个层面是对爱与归属的需求。

sentences.en: Then the need for self-esteem and respect.
sentences.zh: 然后是对自尊和受人尊重的需求。

sentences.en: And then the last, final stage of Maslow's hierarchy is the need for self-actualization.
sentences.zh: 接下来是马斯洛需求层次的最后一个最终阶段，即自我实现的需求。

sentences.en: The desire for fulfillment and being all one can be.
sentences.zh: 对成就感以及发挥个人全部潜能的渴望。

sentences.en: But it's not like Maslow's hierarchy is a video game.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说马斯洛的需求层次就像电子游戏一样。

sentences.en: You don't just neatly complete each level.
sentences.zh: 你并不能轻轻松松地通关每一个级别。

sentences.en: Most members of our society who are normal are partially satisfied in all their basic needs
sentences.zh: 我们社会中大多数正常人在所有基本需求上都部分得到了满足

sentences.en: and partially unsatisfied in all their basic needs at the same time.
sentences.zh: 并且同时在所有基本需求上都部分未得到满足。

sentences.en: Which is to say, a complete gratification hardly ever exists for the wanting animal.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，对于这个不知足的动物来说，彻底的满足几乎从未存在过。

sentences.en: A more realistic description of the hierarchy would be in terms of decreasing percentages of satisfaction
sentences.zh: 对这个层次结构更现实的描述应该是用满足感所占的百分比来衡量，

sentences.en: as we go up the hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 随着我们向层次结构的上方攀升，这个百分比会递减。

sentences.en: We will always have some hunger or another.
sentences.zh: 我们总会面临这样或那样的某种饥渴。

sentences.en: And everything we want and desire in this world is a manifestation of one of these five basic needs.
sentences.zh: 我们在世界上想要和渴望的一切，都是这五种基本需求之一的体现。

sentences.en: A desire for an ice cream cone might actually be an indirect expression of a desire for love.
sentences.zh: 对一个冰淇淋甜筒的渴望实际上可能间接表达了对爱的渴望。

sentences.en: If it is, then this desire for the ice cream cone becomes extremely important motivation.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，那么这种对冰淇淋甜筒的渴望就会变成极其重要的动机。

sentences.en: Every day, conscious desires are to be regarded as symptoms,
sentences.zh: 每天，有意识的渴望都应该被视为一种症状，

sentences.en: as surface indicators of more basic needs.
sentences.zh: 作为更基本需求的表层指标。

sentences.en: Although, sometimes the symptoms of our desires can be so much more complicated,
sentences.zh: 尽管有时我们欲望的症状可能要复杂得多，

sentences.en: so much more elaborate, than an ice cream cone.
sentences.zh: 要精致得多，远不止一个冰淇淋甜筒那么简单。

sentences.en: And what we need manifests in strange and seemingly frivolous ways.
sentences.zh: 而我们的需求会以奇怪且看似轻浮的方式表现出来。

sentences.en: Articles of Interest, our pop-up show about fashion and what we wear, is back.
sentences.zh: “关注的焦点”，我们关于时尚和日常穿搭的快闪节目，又回来了。

sentences.en: We'll be releasing episodes over the next four weeks on Tuesdays and the occasional Fridays,
sentences.zh: 我们将在接下来的四周内，于每周二以及偶尔的周五发布节目，

sentences.en: kind of Tuesday, Friday, Tuesday, Tuesday, Friday, Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 有点像周二、周五、周二、周二、周五、周二这样。

sentences.en: It'll be like the flag of Nepal, but, you know, upside down.
sentences.zh: 它会有点像尼泊尔国旗，但你知道的，是上下颠倒的。

sentences.en: And you don't need to listen to season one to understand season two.
sentences.zh: 你不需要听第一季就能听懂第二季。

sentences.en: You can just dive right in.
But either way, you're already listening to it now.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，你现在已经在收听了。

sentences.en: Articles of Interest, a show about what we wear.
sentences.zh: “关注的焦点”，一档关于我们穿什么的节目。
人们没有意识到这是幻想。

sentences.en: There's always this thing that you have to work extra hard to get.
sentences.zh: 总有些东西需要你付出额外的努力才能得到。

sentences.en: No one dresses like a king anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在没人像国王那样穿衣打扮了。

sentences.en: That's how I make money, love.
sentences.zh: 这就是我赚钱的方式，亲爱的。

sentences.en: There are lots of things that we take for granted that would once have been considered luxuries.
sentences.zh: 有许多我们视为理所当然的事物，在过去会被认为是奢侈品。

sentences.en: I did not love living in the Middle West, the Midwest, and I really wanted to move.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不喜欢在中西部生活，我真的很想搬走。

sentences.en: Linda went to Ohio State University for her master's in art history.
sentences.zh: 琳达在俄亥俄州立大学获得了艺术史硕士学位。

sentences.en: And when she graduated in the early 80s, she was ready to hightail it out to New York or Boston.
sentences.zh: 当她在80年代初毕业时，她已经准备好急匆匆地赶往纽约或波士顿了。
我想要一份博物馆的工作。

sentences.en: But institution after institution, Linda was striking out.
sentences.zh: 但一家又一家机构将琳达拒之门外。

sentences.en: Then, one day, Linda was flipping through a newsletter for museum professionals.
sentences.zh: 然后，有一天，琳达在翻阅一份面向博物馆专业人士的简讯。

sentences.en: And she saw a job listing to be the director at a place in Washington State called the Maryhill Museum of Art.
sentences.zh: 她看到了一条招聘启事，是华盛顿州一个叫玛丽山艺术博物馆的地方在招馆长。

sentences.en: And I thought, what the heck is this?
sentences.zh: 我想，这到底是个什么鬼地方？

sentences.en: And at the time, there was no internet in 1983.
sentences.zh: 而在当时，也就是1983年，还没有互联网。

sentences.en: There was no way to kind of check it up or look at their website.
sentences.zh: 没有什么办法去核实或者查看他们的网站。

sentences.en: I had no idea what this museum was about.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道这个博物馆是做什么的。

sentences.en: But I sent them my materials anyway.
sentences.zh: 但我还是把我的资料寄给了他们。

sentences.en: Even though Linda was 26 years old and had never worked in museum management and didn't know this place at all, she got the job.
sentences.zh: 尽管当时琳达26岁，从未从事过博物馆管理工作，对这个地方也一无所知，但她还是得到了这份工作。

sentences.en: And it was only then that Linda learned exactly where she was moving.
sentences.zh: 直到那时，琳达才知道自己究竟要搬到哪里去。

sentences.en: Maryhill Museum is in the middle of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 玛丽山博物馆位于荒郊野岭之中。

sentences.en: The closest town is Goldendale, Washington, which is 13 miles away.
sentences.zh: 最近的城镇是华盛顿州的戈尔代尔，距离有13英里远。

sentences.en: The Maryhill Museum of Art is a stately mansion perched on top of a cliff by the Columbia River Gorge.
sentences.zh: 玛丽山艺术博物馆是一座宏伟的宅邸，坐落在哥伦比亚河峡谷旁的一处悬崖之巅。

sentences.en: It's stunning, but it looks like it was just cut and pasted onto the Lewis and Clark Trail.
sentences.zh: 它美得惊人，但看起来就像是被人复制粘贴到刘易斯和克拉克小径上的一样。

sentences.en: It has absolutely no other buildings around it.
sentences.zh: 它周围绝对没有任何其他建筑。

sentences.en: It's a very curious place because you drive to it and the museum just unfolds like a castle on the banks of the river, surrounded by basically nothing but hills.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常奇特的地方，因为当你驱车前往时，博物馆就像河岸边的一座城堡一样徐徐展现在眼前，周围基本上除了群山别无他物。

sentences.en: This is not what Linda was picturing when she got into the arts.
sentences.zh: 这并不是琳达当年投身艺术时所想象的画面。

sentences.en: She grew up reading fashion magazines, getting up on culture.
sentences.zh: 她从小读时尚杂志，紧跟文化潮流。

sentences.en: Glamour was kind of my Bible for a long time.
sentences.zh: 有很长一段时间，时尚杂志《魅力》简直就是我的圣经。

sentences.en: I mean, as a teenager, I read every single issue of Seventeen magazine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为一个青少年，我把《十七岁》杂志的每一期都读了。

sentences.en: And then jump cut to Linda at 26 years old, looking out over a vast expanse of the Columbia River.
sentences.zh: 镜头一转，26岁的琳达正眺望着波澜壮阔的哥伦比亚河。

sentences.en: A friend of mine said that she gave me a year because I couldn't live among cowboys.
sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友说，她只给了我一年的期限，因为我无法在牛仔当中生活。

sentences.en: The Maryhill Museum of Art is surrounded by acres and acres of ranch land.
sentences.zh: 玛丽山艺术博物馆四周环绕着数英亩的牧场土地。

sentences.en: Visitors usually found the museum by accident as they were driving back from ski trips.
sentences.zh: 游客们通常是在滑雪回来驾车时偶然发现这个博物馆的。

sentences.en: The closest thing to a restaurant was the nearest gas station.
sentences.zh: 离它最近的餐厅就像是最近的加油站一样。

sentences.en: The closest building at all was two miles away, a small cottage owned by the museum.
sentences.zh: 离它最近的建筑也在两英里之外，那是博物馆拥有的一座小屋。

sentences.en: That's where Linda lived, mostly alone.
sentences.zh: 那就是琳达住的地方，大都独自一人。
你明明是和丈夫一起搬过去的。

sentences.en: My husband was a research glaciologist and he was on expeditions about nine months out of every year.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫是一位研究冰川学的学者，他每年大约有九个月都在外地考察。

sentences.en: So even before our marriage fell apart, I was living alone mostly.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在我们的婚姻破裂之前，我大部分时间也是一个人生活。

sentences.en: So it was mostly just me living there with a big dog.
sentences.zh: 因此，基本上就是我和一条大狗住在那儿。

sentences.en: Linda's big dog was her protector, barking at the rattlesnakes that appeared in her yard and sometimes in her basement.
sentences.zh: 琳达的大狗是她的守护者，它会对出现在她院子里甚至有时出现在她地下室的响尾蛇狂吠。

sentences.en: I was a braver person when I was 26 and stupid.
sentences.zh: 在我26岁还很愚蠢的时候，我可勇敢多了。

sentences.en: As for the collection, what was actually inside the Maryhill Museum of Art, it was all over the place, as random and fascinating as its location.
sentences.zh: 至于馆藏，玛丽山艺术博物馆里究竟有什么，可以说是包罗万象，和它的地理位置一样随性且迷人。

sentences.en: Because the whole museum was created as a lark by four random, fascinating friends.
sentences.zh: 因为整个博物馆是由四个性格各异、魅力十足的朋友出于一时兴起而建立的。

sentences.en: The main founder was businessman Sam Hill.
sentences.zh: 主要的创始人是商人萨姆·希尔。

sentences.en: He began construction on this beautiful mansion in 1914 and named it Maryhill.
sentences.zh: 他在1914年开始建造这座美丽的宅邸，并将其命名为玛丽山。

sentences.en: And there's some debate about whether he named it for his wife or his daughter because they were both named Maryhill.
sentences.zh: 关于他是以妻子的名字还是女儿的名字来命名的，目前还有一些争议，因为她们都叫玛丽山。

sentences.en: Sam Hill roped in friend number two, Loie Fuller, a famous modern dancer, performance artist, and friend to the sculptor Rodin.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·希尔拉上了第二位朋友洛伊·富勒，她是一位著名的现代舞者、行为艺术家，也是雕塑家罗丹的朋友。

sentences.en: She helped bring in a collection of Rodin's original casts to Maryhill.
sentences.zh: 她协助将一批罗丹的原版铸件引入了玛丽山。

sentences.en: The third friend was Queen Marie of Romania.
sentences.zh: 第三位朋友是罗马尼亚的玛丽王后。

sentences.en: She had met Sam Hill in his world travels, and she is why the atrium of the Maryhill Museum of Art is full of beautiful Romanian furniture.
sentences.zh: 她在萨姆·希尔的环球旅行中结识了他，这也是为什么玛丽山艺术博物馆的中庭里摆满了精美的罗马尼亚家具的原因。

sentences.en: And the fourth and most important friend, at least for Linda, was Alma de Bretville Spreckels.
sentences.zh: 而第四位也是最重要的朋友，至少对琳达而言，是阿尔玛·德·布雷特维尔·斯普雷克尔斯。
zh_words: 阿尔玛·德·布雷特维尔·斯普雷克尔斯

sentences.en: She was the wife of Adolf Spreckels, head of the Spreckels Sugar Company.
sentences.zh: 她是斯普雷克尔斯制糖公司负责人阿道夫·斯普雷克尔斯的妻子。

sentences.en: When I was a little girl, the boxes of sugar in our kitchen were always Spreckels sugar.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个小女孩时，我们厨房里的糖盒装的总是斯普雷克尔斯糖。

sentences.en: However, Alma became one of the museum's first trustees and foremost benefactors.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，阿尔玛成为了博物馆的第一批受托人兼最重要的慈善家之一。

sentences.en: Her donation to the museum collection would have the biggest impact on Linda's life.
sentences.zh: 她对博物馆藏品的捐赠将对琳达的生活产生最大的影响。

sentences.en: And it was a bunch of creepy dolls.
sentences.zh: 而那是一堆诡异的玩偶。

sentences.en: I shouldn't say this, but I thought they were the most macabre objects I'd ever seen.
sentences.zh: 我不该这么说，但我认为它们是我见过最毛骨悚然的物品。

sentences.en: When Linda got to Maryhill, she stumbled on a glass case full of these dolls.
sentences.zh: 当琳达来到玛丽山时，她偶然发现了一个摆满这些玩偶的玻璃柜。

sentences.en: And they weren't like baby dolls.
sentences.zh: 它们不像是那种婴儿玩偶。

sentences.en: They were clearly supposed to be adults.
sentences.zh: 它们显然被设定为成年人。

sentences.en: But they were thin and skeletal and looked like they were out of the Nightmare Before Christmas.
sentences.zh: 但它们又瘦又像骨架，看起来像是从《圣诞夜惊魂》里走出来的一样。

sentences.en: Some of them were taken apart, so you'd see a mannequin, a wire mannequin with a disembodied head.
sentences.zh: 其中一些被拆散了，所以你能看到一个人体模特，一个带有独立头颅的铁丝人体模特。

sentences.en: You'd see these parts, little shoes, little purses, these wire bodies, these very blank, ghost-like faces.
sentences.zh: 你能看到这些部件，小鞋子、小钱包、这些铁丝身体，以及那些非常呆滞、宛如幽灵的面孔。

sentences.en: The dolls were 27 inches tall, about double the length of your forearm.
sentences.zh: 这些玩偶高27英寸，大约是你的前臂长度的两倍。

sentences.en: And they all wore strange, dirty dresses and mismatched jackets,
sentences.zh: 它们都穿着奇怪、肮脏的裙子和不搭调的外套，

sentences.en: all bedraggled from years of volunteers playing with them and switching up their outfits.
sentences.zh: 由于多年来志愿者们把玩它们并帮它们更换服装，所有这些衣服都显得破烂不堪。

sentences.en: There were around 50 of these dolls displayed in the glass case,
sentences.zh: 玻璃柜里大约陈列着50个这样的玩偶，

sentences.en: all just bunched up close together like they were on crowded bleachers.
sentences.zh: 它们全都紧紧地挤在一起，就像坐在拥挤的看台上一样。

sentences.en: A bright fluorescent light flickered above them, accentuating their creepiness.
sentences.zh: 一盏明亮的荧光灯在它们上方闪烁，更加突显了它们的诡异感。

sentences.en: Apparently there were about a hundred more of these dolls in storage.
sentences.zh: 显然，仓库里还有大约一百个这样的玩偶。

sentences.en: Linda did not know what was up with these dolls.
sentences.zh: 琳达不知道这些玩偶是怎么回事。

sentences.en: But she couldn't really dwell on it.
sentences.zh: 但她也没有办法过多纠结此事。

sentences.en: Frankly, there were so many things that had to be done at Maryhill.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，玛丽山有太多事情亟待处理。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, absolutely everything was in some sort of disrepair or dysfunction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，绝对每一样东西都处于某种失修或瘫痪的状态。

sentences.en: I mean, from the bathrooms to signage.
sentences.zh: 我是说，从洗手间到指示牌。

sentences.en: So, among the Rodana sculptures, the Romanian furniture,
sentences.zh: 所以，在罗丹的雕塑、罗马尼亚的家具、

sentences.en: a large collection of indigenous art and a display of chess sets,
sentences.zh: 大量本土艺术收藏以及一组国际象棋展示之间，
摆放着这些肮脏的玩偶，

sentences.en: piling up against the glass showcase in the hall, collecting duSt.
sentences.zh: 它们堆在大厅的玻璃展柜旁，积满了灰尘。

sentences.en: Until one day, when Linda got a call from a curator at the DeYoung Museum in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，琳达接到了旧金山德扬博物馆一位馆长的电话。

sentences.en: She asked Linda if she could come to Maryhill because she wanted to see these dolls.
sentences.zh: 她问琳达是否可以来玛丽山，因为她想看看这些玩偶。

sentences.en: And that was when Linda learned what she had on her hands.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，琳达才知道了她手里掌握着什么宝贝。

sentences.en: These dolls weren't supposed to be so macabre.
sentences.zh: 这些玩偶本不该如此毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Actually, they were kind of heroes in a way.
sentences.zh: 事实上，从某种意义上说，它们算得上是英雄。

sentences.en: Because these dolls had saved French fashion.
sentences.zh: 因为这些玩偶拯救了法国时尚。

sentences.en: This is the end of German pride and power in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这是德国在巴黎的傲慢与权力的终结。

sentences.en: It began with the fall of France,
sentences.zh: 这一切始于法国的沦陷，

sentences.en: and now amid the jeers of the people, the Nazi has fallen.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在人们的嘲笑声中，纳粹已经倒台。

sentences.en: After four devastating years of Nazi occupation,
sentences.zh: 经过四年毁灭性的纳粹占领之后，

sentences.en: Feast of Liberation at the Paris Opera of Long Renown
sentences.zh: 巴黎歌剧院里举行了闻名遐迩的解放庆典，

sentences.en: and all through the city, the same sights and sounds.
sentences.zh: 整个城市都充斥着同样的景象与声音。

sentences.en: Ecstatic, Parisians rejoiced in the streets.
sentences.zh: 欣喜若狂的巴黎人在街头欢庆。

sentences.en: Some of them gathered up the ration tickets that had governed their lives
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人收集起曾主宰他们生活的配给券，

sentences.en: And this turned out to be a very bad idea,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这真是一个极其糟糕的主意，

sentences.en: because the war was not over.
They'd still need those ration tickets.
sentences.zh: 他们依然需要那些粮票。

sentences.en: In the aftermath of the occupation,
more than five million French adults and children
sentences.zh: 超过五百万的法国成年人和儿童

sentences.en: didn't have adequate shelter or food.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的庇护所或食物。

sentences.en: Parisians, dressed in ratty, worn clothes,
sentences.zh: 巴黎人穿着破旧磨损的衣服，

sentences.en: walked and bicycled through their dark city.
